name: Huaji (滑稽) emoji
blurb: The smirking round-face emoji from Baidu Tieba, used for sly irony and trolling
title: Huaji (滑稽) Emoji Meme: Meaning, Origin & Use
description: Huaji (滑稽) is a smirking round face with side-eyes and pink cheeks from Baidu Tieba. Widely used by 2012, it signals sly irony in Chinese chat.
h1: What is the Huaji (滑稽) emoji?
answer: Huaji (滑稽, "funny" or "comical") is a round yellow face with pink cheeks, raised eyebrows, eyes glancing to the side and a small knowing smile. It started as a sticker on Baidu Tieba, China's big forum network, where it was first called 斜眼笑 (side-eye smile), and was already in wide use there by 2012. Because it can mean amusement, sarcasm, innocence and mischief all at once, it became one of the best-loved Chinese reaction faces, with plush pillows, color variants and a place in WeChat's built-in emoji in 2016.

sections.h: What it looks like and means
body: Picture a smiley whose eyes slide to one side while the mouth curls up a little: the look of someone who knows exactly what they are doing. Posted after a comment, it says "I'm being sly", "just kidding" or "you know what I mean".

When the image is not available, people type 手动滑稽 ("manual huaji") or （滑稽） in brackets to get the same effect in words. It sits close to the doge face (狗头) as a sarcasm marker, but huaji is more about cheeky amusement than covering yourself.

head: Date
Event
rows: The face appears in Baidu Tieba's sticker set under the name 斜眼笑 and goes through several redesigns
Already widely used across Tieba, especially in heated threads, for its mix of meanings
Huaji-face pillows become a hit on Taobao and go on sale on Amazon Japan
WeChat adds a huaji-style face to its built-in emoji on iOS
During a Baidu campaign, Tieba temporarily blocks the huaji code; it returns afterwards

ul: After an obvious exaggeration: "I studied for ten whole minutes [huaji]"
To soften a jab: "Nice drawing, very abstract [huaji]"
Typed as （手动滑稽） when the sticker is missing
Colored versions (red, orange, green, blue, purple) and remixed faces in sticker packs
As a fandom symbol: Tieba even has a forum dedicated to the face

body: Huaji is a classic of Chinese internet culture. It is less dominant than in the Tieba era, but it is still built into apps and sticker packs and instantly understood. It is not part of Unicode, so it does not appear in standard emoji keyboards outside Chinese platforms.

faq.a: Literally "funny" or "comical". As an emoji it signals a sly, teasing or ironic tone.
"Manual huaji": typing the word instead of posting the sticker, to mark a comment as a joke.

faq.q: Is huaji the same as doge?
faq.a: No. Both mark irony, but huaji is a smirking smiley from Baidu Tieba, while 狗头 is the Shiba Inu doge face used to say "I'm only joking".
